Major costs and financial risks: Commodity prices, extraction, energy and processing costs
Notes: Commodity spending is not specific to AI and also serves other industries.

Who pays: Wafer manufacturers, chip manufacturers and packaging firms
Who receives the spending: Silicon, wafer, chemical and industrial-gas suppliers
Major costs and financial risks: Purification, plant investment, quality control and qualification
Notes: Qualified materials can command value beyond their raw commodity content.

Economic layer: Chip design and electronic design automation (EDA)
Who receives the spending: EDA vendors, IP licensors and design-service providers
Major costs and financial risks: Engineering, research, software licenses and IP royalties
Notes: Design firms may also earn revenue from chip sales downstream. This row covers design inputs.

Who pays: Foundries, memory producers and other chip manufacturers
Who receives the spending: ASML, Applied Materials, Lam Research, KLA and other equipment vendors
Major costs and financial risks: Research, complex manufacturing, service networks and customer investment cycles
Notes: Equipment sales and installed-base service revenue are distinct streams.

Who pays: Fabless chip designers and companies outsourcing production
Who receives the spending: Foundries such as TSMC and Samsung, and Intel Foundry where contracted
Major costs and financial risks: Fab construction, depreciation, yield, utilization and process development
Notes: Illustrative roles do not imply that each named foundry manufactures for every chip designer. Internal manufacturing transfers differ from external sales.

Who pays: Chip designers, manufacturers and system builders, depending on the contract
Who receives the spending: SK hynix, Samsung, Micron and packaging providers
Major costs and financial risks: Capacity investment, stacking and integration yield, and demand cycles
Notes: High-bandwidth memory (HBM) purchases and packaging-service payments can involve different counterparties.

Who pays: Cloud operators, enterprises, governments and system builders
Who receives the spending: Accelerator vendors, server manufacturers and networking suppliers
Major costs and financial risks: Hardware development, inventory, supply commitments and obsolescence
Notes: A system purchase can contain revenue already recognized at upstream layers; revenues cannot simply be added as economic value.

Who pays: Model developers, enterprises and application companies
Who receives the spending: Cloud providers, colocation operators and infrastructure suppliers
Major costs and financial risks: Accelerators, construction, electricity, cooling, utilization and financing
Notes: Equity and debt fund investment but are not customer revenue. Owners, operators and cloud-service providers can be different entities.

Who pays: API customers, subscribers and enterprise clients
Who receives the spending: Model developers and hosting or distribution partners
Major costs and financial risks: Training, inference, data, talent, research and customer acquisition
Notes: Investor funding is financing rather than revenue. Open-weight releases may support indirect monetization.

Who receives the spending: Software vendors, AI startups and enterprise platforms
Major costs and financial risks: Model and compute usage, engineering, integration, sales and support
Notes: Some products are bundled or advertising-funded; not all use a separate subscription.

Who receives the spending: Application vendors, cloud providers and implementation partners
Major costs and financial risks: Subscriptions, usage charges, integration, training and organizational change
Notes: Users receive services and possible productivity benefits, not necessarily income. This row shows final demand, not an additional production layer.
